text: Characterization: given attachments using only content_base64/content_text, graph_send_mail accepts and sends them with zero correctness check against the stated filename -- the structural gap this design's content_url mechanism is built to avoid (no source-of-truth check is possible for inline content).
Given content_url pointing to an allow-listed host serving content under the per-file size cap, When graph_send_mail is called, Then the mail is sent with exactly the fetched bytes as the attachment.
Given content_url whose host is not on the allow-list, When graph_send_mail is called, Then the tool returns invalid_argument naming the rejected host, and no Graph request is made.
Given the default empty allow-list, When any attachment specifies content_url, Then it is rejected with invalid_argument stating the feature is not configured, and no Graph request is made.
Given the content_url fetch returns HTTP 500, When graph_send_mail is called, Then the tool returns upstream_error (retryable=true), and no Graph request is made.
Given the content_url fetch returns HTTP 404, When graph_send_mail is called, Then the tool returns not_found (retryable=false), and no Graph request is made.

Given the content_url fetch succeeds but returns content over _MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, When graph_send_mail is called, Then the existing size-limit error fires citing the actual fetched byte count, and no Graph request is made.

Given an attachment specifies both content_text and content_url (or content_base64 and content_url), When graph_send_mail is called, Then the tool returns invalid_argument ("needs exactly one of"), and no Graph request is made.

Given attachments using only content_text or content_base64 exactly as before (PRD-19661/PRD-20416), When graph_send_mail is called, Then behavior and response shape are byte-for-byte identical to pre-change.

Given a successful send with one or more attachments (any source), When the call completes, Then the server logs one entry per attachment with filename, decoded byte length, sha256 and source (inline|url).

Given a real HTTPS URL on an allow-listed test host and a live Graph test mailbox, When the mail is sent with content_url pointing at that URL, Then the mail received carries an attachment whose sha256 matches the source file's sha256 exactly.
steps: Stand up or pick a test HTTPS host and add it to ATTACHMENT_FETCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS for this run
Place a known file (e.g. a sample report .html) at a URL on that host; record its sha256
Call graph_send_mail against a live Graph test mailbox with one attachment: {filename, content_url: <that URL>}
Open the received mail in the test mailbox and download the attachment
Compute sha256 of the downloaded attachment
expect: Downloaded attachment's sha256 exactly equals the source file's recorded sha256; filename matches what was specified.
